division.heading: Discharge of sewage in the Antarctic Area or Arctic waters

content.p: Unless the contrary intention appears, an expression that is used in this Division and in Annex IV to the Convention (whether or not a particular meaning is given to it by that Annex) has, in this Division, the same meaning as in that Annex.
The object of this Division is to give effect to Australia’s obligations regarding the discharge of sewage in the Antarctic Area or Arctic waters under Annex IV to the Convention and the Polar Code.
Fault-based offences
A person commits an offence if:
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct causes a discharge of sewage from a ship in the Antarctic Area; and
the person is reckless or negligent as to causing the discharge by that conduct; and
the ship is a ship to which Annex IV to the Convention applies; and
if the discharge occurs outside the outer limits of the exclusive economic zone adjacent to the coast of the Australian Antarctic Territory—the ship is an Australian ship.
Penalty: 2,000 penalty units.
A person commits an offence if:
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct causes a discharge of sewage from a ship in Arctic waters; and
the person is reckless or negligent as to causing the discharge by that conduct; and
the ship is a ship to which Annex IV to the Convention applies; and
the ship is an Australian ship.
Penalty: 2,000 penalty units.
Strict liability offences
The master and the owner of a ship each commit an offence of strict liability if:
sewage is discharged from the ship in the Antarctic Area; and
the ship is a ship to which Annex IV to the Convention applies; and
if the discharge occurs outside the outer limits of the exclusive economic zone adjacent to the coast of the Australian Antarctic Territory—the ship is an Australian ship.
Penalty: 500 penalty units.
The master and the owner of a ship each commit an offence of strict liability if:
sewage is discharged from the ship in Arctic waters; and
the ship is a ship to which Annex IV to the Convention applies; and
the ship is an Australian ship.
Penalty: 500 penalty units.
Exception—discharge of sewage for ship’s safety etc.
Subsections (3) and (4) do not apply to the discharge of sewage from a ship if:
the discharge is necessary for the purpose of:
securing the safety of the ship and persons on board the ship; or
saving life at sea; or
both of the following apply:
the discharge results from damage to the ship or its equipment;
all reasonable precautions were taken before and after the occurrence of the damage for the purpose of preventing or minimising the discharge.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (5): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Exception—discharge of comminuted and disinfected sewage etc.
Without limiting the generality of subsection (5), subsections (3) and (4) do not apply to the discharge of sewage from a ship if the following conditions are satisfied:
the ship is not a category A ship, category B ship or passenger ship constructed on or after 1 January 2017;

if the sewage has been comminuted and disinfected using a system approved in accordance with the regulations, or orders made pursuant to the regulations, giving effect to paragraph 1.2 of Regulation 9 of Annex IV to the Convention—the discharge is made when the ship is:
as far as practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10; and
at a distance of more than 3 nautical miles from the nearest land, any ice-shelf or fast ice;
if the sewage has not been comminuted or disinfected using such a system—the discharge is made when the ship is:
as far as practicable from areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10; and
at a distance of more than 12 nautical miles from the nearest land, any ice-shelf or fast ice;

if the sewage has been stored in a holding tank or originates from spaces containing living animals—the sewage is not discharged instantaneously but is discharged at a prescribed rate when the ship is proceeding en route at a speed of not less than 4 knots.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (6): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Exception—discharge of sewage treated in sewage treatment plant
Without limiting the generality of subsection (5), subsections (3) and (4) do not apply to the discharge of sewage from a ship if the following conditions are satisfied:
the sewage has been treated in a sewage treatment plant on the ship;
an inspector has certified that the sewage treatment plant meets the requirements of the regulations giving effect to paragraph 1.1 or 2.1 of Regulation 9 of Annex IV to the Convention;
the discharge is made when the ship is as far as practicable from the nearest land, any ice-shelf, fast ice or areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10;
the effluent does not produce visible floating solids in the Antarctic Area or Arctic waters and does not cause discolouration in the Antarctic Area or Arctic waters.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (7): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Without limiting the generality of subsection (5), subsections (3) and (4) do not apply to the discharge of sewage from a ship if the following conditions are satisfied:
the ship is a category A ship or category B ship operating in areas of ice concentration exceeding 1/10 for extended periods of time;
the sewage has been treated in a sewage treatment plant on the ship;
an inspector has certified that the sewage treatment plant meets the requirements of the regulations giving effect to paragraph 1.1 or 2.1 of Regulation 9 of Annex IV to the Convention;
the discharge has been approved in accordance with the regulations.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (8): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
Exception—discharge of sewage in territorial waters of foreign country

Without limiting the generality of subsection (5), subsections (3) and (4) do not apply to the discharge of sewage from a ship if the discharge occurs in the territorial waters of a foreign country in accordance with the law of that country.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to the matter in subsection (9): see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code.
